title.narrative: Revenue Improvement and Spending Efficiency Program-for-Results Operation

description.narrative: The Revenue Improvement and Spending Efficiency (RISE) Operation aims to enhance revenue mobilization and promote efficient public investment in Rwanda. The Program is organized around three results areas (RA) to support the government's efforts to increase domestic revenue collection (RA 1) and make public investment and asset management more efficient and transparent at the national (RA 2) and subnational (RA 3) levels. The expected outcomes will be measured with the following indicators: (i) tax-to-GDP ratio is increased, (ii) percentage of central government procurement contracts that are signed within the initial bid validity period of 120 days, (iii) annual financial statements of SOCs and criteria for the allocation of subsidies to SOCs are published online, (iv) districts publish annual budget performance reports online, and (v) number of new and improved jobs expected through LED projects included in the budget. The Program builds on the World Bank's long history of partnership with the Government of Rwanda in PFM reform. This includes previous efforts to ensure that PFM systems are responsive to the emerging needs of climate change, fiscal space consolidation, and greater demand for an inclusive approach to development. It is anchored in the PFM Sector Strategic Plan (SSP) and the Governance and Decentralization SSP for 2024-2029. These strategies constitute the cornerstones of the Government's public finance and decentralization reform agenda and will expand and deepen the ongoing reforms under the Second National Strategic Transformation (NST-2). Accordingly, it will be implemented by the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning in collaboration with the Ministry of Local Governments. The Program will also leverage existing PFM and decentralization structures, including Sector Working Groups. Technical assistance will be provided through an Investment Project Financing component.
To enhance domestic revenue collection and improve the efficiency, transparency, and job creation potential of public spending

title.narrative: Major projects included in the budget meet spending and implementation milestones per published feasibility studies

baseline.value: There are no standardized guidelines for conducting feasibility studies. Feasibility studies for some major projects are published online (receiving a B score in the PEFA 2022 assessment performance indicator 11.1). Quarterly and annual progress reports are prepared but not published (receiving a C score in the PEFA 2022 assessment performance indicator 11.4). Major projects entering the FY26 budget will be tracked for adherence to spending and implementation timelines per their feasibility studies.

target.value: All major projects have published feasibility studies and all quarterly and annual implementation progress reports are published (corresponding to a PEFA assessment score of A and B, respectively). All major projects that entered the budget in FY26 achieve spending and implementation milestones within a 10 percent variation.
